🗓
October 7 marks
the 24th anniversary of the signing of
the Charter of the Collective Security Treaty Organisation
(
#CSTO
), the instrument that established the CSTO as an international regional association.
Its
stated purposes
– the strengthening of peace and stability and the collective defence of the independence, territorial integrity and sovereignty of the member states –
remain the cornerstone of mutually beneficial cooperation in a true spirit of alliance
.
On this basis,
the Russian Federation assumed the CSTO
chairmanship
in 2026
under the motto
‘Collective Security in a
#MultipolarWorld
: A Common Goal, a Shared Responsibility’.
In a short span by historical standards, the Organisation, which today brings together six states –
Russia, Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan
– has made substantial headway and established itself as
a key mechanism for safeguarding regional security
.
The CSTO systematically
addresses the prevention and settlement of crises
and
counters the many challenges and threats to stability
. It continually enhances the combat readiness of the organisation’s Collective Forces and
sustains intensive foreign-policy coordination
.
Drawing upon its considerable experience and advanced security instruments,
the CSTO continues to evolve
, adapting flexibly to changing circumstances.
🛡
In order to strengthen the Organisation’s security capabilities,
the unique combat experience of
the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation
is being drawn upon
– including in
exercises involving the CSTO Collective Forces
held in the Chelyabinsk Region in September and October 2026.
Cooperation in the emerging fields of biological and information security
is likewise gathering pace. Operations conducted by the law-enforcement agencies and security services of the member states to combat
terrorism, illicit drug trafficking, illegal migration and cybercrime
continue to deliver substantial results.
🤝
The development of ties with other international organisations is a key strand of the CSTO member states’ systematic efforts
. Since 2004, the Organisation has held
observer status
at the UN General Assembly.
Priority is being given to deepening cooperation with the CIS and the SCO
, and the roadmap for cooperation among the three organisations in areas of mutual interest continues to be implemented.
A joint conference of the CSTO, CIS and SCO
on security issues in Central Asia and Afghanistan will be held in Moscow on October 15-16.
The memory of
the Soviet Union’s Victory in the Great Patriotic War
remains a cornerstone of our allied cooperation and of our shared enduring values
. The CSTO member states are joining forces to preserve the truth about the heroism of the Soviet people and to prevent any rewriting of history or any distortion or revision of the war’s outcome.
Prospects for expanding multifaceted allied cooperation will be discussed at the forthcoming
session of the CSTO Collective Security Council,
and at
the joint meeting of the Organisation’s Council of Foreign Ministers, Council of Defence Ministers and Committee of Secretaries of Security Councils
. Both will be held in Moscow on November 10-11. Decisions aimed at strengthening the CSTO collective security system are to be signed.
❗️
The further expansion of comprehensive cooperation with the CSTO member States is
a priority of the Russian Federation’s foreign policy
.

item.title: 🇷🇺 On October 7, Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Turkmenistan Rashid Meredov
item.description: 🇷🇺 🇹🇲 On October 7, Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Turkmenistan Rashid Meredov held talks on the sidelines of the CIS Council of Foreign Ministers. 👉 Sergey Lavrov’s opening remarks The Ministers reaffirmed their mutual readiness to continue working together and coordinating closely in various international forums , including the Commonwealth of Independent States, dialogue among the Caspian littoral states and the #RussiaCentralAsia format. During the meeting, the Ministers discussed key issues on the Russia-Turkmenistan agenda and reaffirmed their shared commitment to strengthening bilateral relations, which enjoy the high status of an enhanced strategic partnership. They exchanged views on further developing cultural, humanitarian and educational tie s, as well as cooperation within the Intergovernmental Russian-Turkmen Commission on Economic Cooperation . Sergey Lavrov and Rashid Meredov signed a plan for consultations between the two countries’ Foreign Ministries for 2027-2028. 🤝 The talks took place in a traditionally friendly atmosphere of mutual trust . #RussiaTurkmenistan

On October 7, Russia and the Lao People’s Democratic Republic celebrate the
6️⃣
6️⃣
th Anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations.
Bilateral ties between Moscow and Vientiane are rooted in
long-standing traditions of friendship and cooperation
and are characterised by a high level of trust.
Our country provided significant assistance to the Lao people
in their struggle for national liberation, as well as in building national statehood, developing the economy and strengthening the country’s defence capabilities.
***
🤝
#Laos
is a reliable partner of Russia in the
#AsiaPacific
.
The foundation of our bilateral relations is the Treaty on the Principles of Friendly Relations, signed on March 9, 1994. In October 2011,
Russia and Laos adopted the
Declaration on Strategic Partnership in the Asia-Pacific Region.
Russia-Lao ties are multifaceted.
Political dialogue at the highest and high levels is maintained on a regular basis.
Inter-parliamentary ties are developing
actively, while exchanges of delegations between relevant ministries and agencies are expanding.
📈
Trade and economic ties are steadily growing.
Last year, bilateral trade doubled compared to 2024. The Inter-governmental Commission operates on a regular basis.
One of the priority areas of bilateral cooperation is the development of
military and military-technical cooperation.
Interaction in the fields of security and law enforcement is also gaining momentum.
Cultural
and
humanitarian
exchanges
are being expanded, while joint initiatives in education are being promoted, including
support for the Russian language in Laos.
More than 10'000 Lao nationals have received education at Soviet and Russian universities. Many graduates have been promoted to senior positions in the country’s Party and state apparatus, the Command Staff of the Lao People’s Army and law enforcement agencies.
President of the Lao People’s Democratic Republic, Comrade
Thongloun Sisoulith
is a graduate of the Leningrad Pedagogical Institute.
Prime
Minister
—
Comrade Saleumxay
Kommasith
— graduated from
MGIMO University.
In his previous capacity as Minister of Foreign Affairs, he visited our country on numerous occasions, attended the St Petersburg International Economic Forum.
🌐
Russia and Laos have
similar
or
identical
positions
on key international issues, enabling effective cooperation within leading international and regional frameworks.
We share a commitment to building a fairer and more democratic
#MultipolarWorld
based on the principles of the
#UNCharter
, including the principle of sovereign equality of all states —
#UNCharterIsOurRules
.
Moscow and Vientiane continue their constructive cooperation within
#ASEAN
and ASEAN-centred mechanisms. The Lao Side has expressed its readiness to join the activities of the
#SCO
as a dialogue partner.
💬
President of Russia
Vladimir
Putin
, during his
meeting at the Kremlin
with
President of Laos Thongloun Sisoulith
, who came to Russia to take part in the
#VictoryDay
celebrations
(May 9, 2026):
Our relations are built and continue to develop on the
basis of friendship, mutual respect and trust.
<…>
We are actively working together on the international stage.
New opportunities for cooperation are also opening up following your country’s obtaining the status of a dialogue partner of the
#SCO
.
🎉
We congratulate our Lao colleagues and friends on this shared Anniversary and look forward to further strengthening Russian-Lao friendship and developing bilateral relations.
#RussiaLaos

item.title: 🇷🇺 #Announcement On October 8-9, President of Russia Vladimir Putin will pay a working visit to Turkmenistan
item.description: #Announcement 🇷🇺 🇹🇲 On October 8-9, President of Russia Vladimir Putin will pay a working visit to Turkmenistan . The Russian President will take part in a meeting of the CIS Council of Heads of State and the Caspian Environmental Summit , both to be held in Turkmenistan’s Avaza National Tourist Zone. At the meeting of the CIS Council of Heads of State, the Leaders will review cooperation among the member states as the Commonwealth marks its 35th anniversary this year, set priorities for further joint work and exchange views on current international and regional issues. ✍️ Documents are expected to be adopted to expand cooperation in law enforcement, culture, humanitarian affairs and information, as well as to strengthen foreign policy coordination among the CIS countries. At the Caspian Environmental Summit, the Presidents of Russia, Azerbaijan, Iran, Kazakhstan and Turkmenistan will discuss practical aspects of environmental cooperation among the Caspian littoral states , including measures to prevent the decline in the Caspian Sea’s water level and preserve its biological resources. 🤝 During his visit to Turkmenistan, Vladimir Putin will hold a series of bilateral meetings .

item.content:encoded:

🎙
Remarks and answers to media questions
by Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov at a joint press conference with Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Timor-Leste Bendito Freitas
(Moscow, October 6, 2026)
💬
Sergey Lavrov:
Our talks took place in a friendly atmosphere and were
very productive
.
Before today’s meeting, we had met on the sidelines of international events in previous years. Today, we thoroughly discussed
the current state and prospects of our bilateral relations
, as well as
the international agenda
.
We share an interest in developing and expanding cooperation
, preferably as swiftly and effectively as possible, in line with
the agreements
reached by President of Russia
Vladimir Putin
and Prime Minister of Timor-Leste
Xanana Gusmao
during their meeting in Kazan this June, on the sidelines of
the #RussiaASEAN anniversary Summit
marking 35 years of our partnership with the Association.
We have made very little progress in trade and economic ties so far, but today’s discussions confirmed some promising prospects.
Both Sides are keen to explore joint investment projects in energy, mining, fisheries and tourism.
We discussed dialogue between our ministries on foreign policy issues
. The Minister proposed holding regular consultations, and we supported this proposal. We will draw up a plan for these contacts, which I believe will be very useful.
I briefed my colleague on the latest developments surrounding Ukraine
. I emphasised the need for a lasting settlement of this crisis by addressing its
well-known root causes
.
***
Key points from the answers to media questions
:
• When we issued
a very clear statement
in response to
threats by the Baltic states
and other NATO members that had “got out of hand” to attack the Kaliningrad Region,
we were immediately assured
– by both NATO Secretary General
Mark Rutte
and US Permanent Representative to NATO
Matthew Whitaker
–
that the bloc had no plans to attack Russia
and could not possibly have any, since NATO was supposedly a defensive alliance.
• We have heard many times that NATO is a defensive alliance
, but that did not save
Yugoslavia
,
Afghanistan
or
Libya
.
• NATO members are now trying to extend their military presence to the Far East, Southeast Asia and Northeast Asia. My colleague and I discussed this today. We hear what they say, but, as the Russian saying goes, we
“keep our ears pricked”
. Above all, we are working to fulfil the objectives set by President
Vladimir Putin
for
the special military operation
–
to prevent any threats to the Russian Federation from our western neighbours.
• At
the Valdai Forum
, President
Vladimir Putin
gave an unambiguous answer to the question of what would happen if the Kaliningrad Region were attacked.
He made it clear that if the Kaliningrad Region or any other region of the Russian Federation were attacked, the response would be the same.
